terms.label: Parent scaffold
terms.definition: Reusable definitions, composition and verification mechanisms shared by consumers; selected organization or project workflow choices live in profiles.
examples: One parent package serves strict-release and synthetic-trunk.

terms.label: Profile
terms.definition: An approved named set of workflow policy values and permitted project customizations selected for a declared scope.
examples: One profile targets develop; another permits feature branches to target main.

terms.label: Project
terms.definition: A declared consumer scope with canonical repository identities, a selected profile and explicit composition inputs.
examples: A project declares its repository and binds a project review procedure.

terms.label: Policy
terms.definition: Approved criteria governing an operation, including permitted configuration and required evidence; policy does not grant platform permissions.
examples: The selected policy requires a ticket identifier on accepted commits.

terms.label: Effective policy
terms.definition: The deterministic result of resolving approved parent, organization and project policy inputs, with provenance and a revision or digest. Evaluate a policy-changing operation under the previously approved policy, not its proposed replacement.
examples: An explanation reports the controlling ticket syntax and its approved source.

terms.label: Policy override
terms.definition: An explicit change to a policy field that the controlling approved layer permits a lower layer to customize.
examples: A permitted project setting chooses a different ticket syntax.

terms.label: Skill
terms.definition: A scoped procedure or reference resource selected for a task; reading or replacing its prose cannot create permission or approval.
examples: A code review skill supplies a review procedure.

terms.label: Procedure binding
terms.definition: An explicit association between a task procedure role and the qualified skill selected to perform it.
examples: The review role selects a project-specific review skill.

terms.label: Skill replacement
terms.definition: An explicit composition declaration selecting a qualified skill instead of another for the declared procedure role and scope.
examples: The default review procedure is replaced across explicit and prerequisite routes.

terms.label: Skill extension
terms.definition: An explicit composition declaration adding scoped skill content in a declared order while retaining the referenced base procedure.
examples: A project review adds a notebook check after the general review.

terms.label: Resident block
terms.definition: A stable identified section of instructions selected to remain in the active resident context.
examples: A workflow block carries the selected project topology.

terms.label: Resident composition
terms.definition: Deterministic assembly of parent and project resident blocks using declared replacement or extension, provenance and a final size budget. Every managed output must identify the same approved parent lock; mixed parent inputs are invalid.
examples: A project replaces its workflow block and preserves common integrity blocks.

terms.label: Repository identity
terms.definition: Canonical host, owner and repository identifiers used to identify the actual operation target repository. Directory or file applicability is a separate scope bound to that identity. Missing, foreign or ambiguous identity remains unknown and cannot inherit a neighboring project.
examples: Equal repository basenames under different owners do not identify the same target.

terms.label: Applicability scope
terms.definition: The targets and operation classes for which a policy, skill or check is relevant.
examples: A notebook check applies only to the declared project and notebook changes.

terms.label: Authorization scope
terms.definition: The actors, resources, operations and validity limits covered by an actual authorization.
examples: Permission to inspect one repository does not grant deployment authority.

terms.label: Host capability
terms.definition: A specific mechanism a pinned host/backend combination can provide, with capability evidence recorded separately from configuration.
examples: Tool-call denial and instruction delivery are separate host capabilities.

terms.label: Host adapter
terms.definition: The implementation that maps structured inputs and decisions to a particular host protocol and observes its outcome.
examples: An adapter translates a denial into the supported tool-interception response.

terms.label: Gate
terms.definition: A check that evaluates operation facts and evidence against applicable policy at a declared boundary and returns a decision.
examples: A ticket gate inspects actual commit messages in the candidate range.

terms.label: Evidence
terms.definition: An observable record supporting a specific claim, bound to relevant source, target, revision, method and validity conditions.
examples: A canary records the exact adapter revision and the prevented side effect.

terms.label: Authorization record
terms.definition: A record of permission or an approved scoped exception from an authorized issuer, with scope and validity; the record cannot create its own issuer authority. A project-scoped exception cannot extend to another project or weaken the common integrity floor.
examples: An approved exception identifies its issuer, allowed operation and expiration.

terms.label: Parent lock
terms.definition: An immutable reference to the approved parent source and compatible artifacts, including revision and provenance needed to detect mixed inputs.
examples: Skills and runtime artifacts identify the same parent commit and compatible build.

terms.label: Rollback receipt
terms.definition: A record identifying the exact previous compatible artifact and policy set and the state compatibility needed to restore it. The target is a previously approved exact lock and effective-policy digest, never a live branch or tag tip.
examples: Rollback names the prior immutable set and invalidates incompatible task evidence.

terms.label: Configured
terms.definition: A declared setting or registration exists for an identified target; this fact alone says nothing about artifact presence or observed behavior.
examples: Settings name a hook command that has not yet been installed or observed.

terms.label: Generated
terms.definition: An artifact was produced from identified inputs; generation alone does not establish installation, runtime execution or acceptance protection.
examples: A build emits a hook manifest into its output tree.

terms.label: Installed
terms.definition: Identified artifacts are present at the intended consumer locations; installation alone does not prove the host executes them.
examples: A hook file is present at its configured path.

terms.label: Configuration valid
terms.definition: A named configuration passed its declared structural and consistency checks at an exact revision.
examples: A schema check rejects unknown fields and accepts the two valid profile fixtures.

terms.label: Artifact verified
terms.definition: An identified artifact set passed declared provenance, content and compatibility checks; this is a scoped artifact claim.
examples: Installed file hashes match the approved package and project composition.

terms.label: Runtime observed
terms.definition: The declared behavior was actually exercised through the identified registered path in a pinned runtime, with the outcome recorded.
examples: An allowed operation succeeds and a denial canary leaves its target unchanged.

terms.label: Acceptance blocking
terms.definition: Observed protection at a declared acceptance boundary actually prevents an invalid candidate from being accepted, with exact candidate/range and protection configuration bound to the evidence.
examples: Protected checks reject a candidate containing an invalid commit even when local hooks were bypassed.

terms.label: Common integrity floor
terms.definition: Shared requirements for authorization, credential handling, work preservation and evidence integrity; selected workflow topology is defined separately in profiles.
examples: Replacing a project workflow does not waive credential handling or invent approval.

terms.label: Source reference
terms.definition: A repository locator and revision expression; a branch or tag name alone is mutable and does not establish an immutable parent lock.
examples: Resolve a branch to its exact approved commit before generating or activating artifacts.

terms.label: Generated artifact
terms.definition: Output derived from identified source inputs and a generator version; provenance and verification are separate recorded properties.
examples: A generated resident file records the parent and project inputs used to compose it.

terms.label: Activation receipt
terms.definition: A record of the coherent artifact and policy set actually activated, its validation evidence and prior compatible state; it is not new authorization.
examples: Activation records the new parent lock and policy digest plus the prior rollback target.

terms.label: Local feedback
terms.definition: A locally executed check or diagnostic that may prevent a normal local operation but can be bypassed outside its declared local boundary.
examples: A native commit hook rejects a missing ticket; bypassing that hook remains possible.

terms.label: Content publisher
terms.definition: A namespace identifying the source of selected skills and resident instructions. Publisher ownership is distinct from project scope, profile adoption and observed host capability; publication grants no authorization.
examples: Siege supplies a reference bundle while an independent project keeps its own workflow profile.

terms.label: Content selection
terms.definition: An explicit configured set of publisher sources, procedure edges, routes and resident blocks consumed by the shared composer. It may reference the separately approved policy but cannot adopt, replace or authorize that policy.
examples: A project selects a Siege formatting skill without adopting Siege ticket or branch requirements.

terms.label: Content bundle
terms.definition: A selected, versioned set of publisher-owned content and its descriptor, pinned separately from scaffold and project sources. Its profile requirements diagnose missing adoption; selecting it establishes no policy authority or host capability.
examples: bundles/siege/build-bundle.json describes the bounded Siege composition content.

terms.label: Selected registration
terms.definition: An explicit local binding of verified selected package bytes, backend, repository identity and independently pinned policy and adapter inputs to settings and native Git hooks. A configured receipt grants no provider or protected acceptance authority. Interrupted publication is unusable until recovery.
examples: The claude-code-local installer rebuilds immutable selected inputs before registering a disposable repository.

relationships.subject: project
relationships.definition: Selection is scoped to the declared project identity.

relationships.subject: profile
relationships.definition: Only approved values and permitted overrides participate.

relationships.subject: gate
relationships.definition: The gate uses operation facts and separately supplied evidence.

relationships.subject: host-adapter
relationships.definition: Implementation presence does not establish observed capability.

relationships.subject: procedure-binding
relationships.definition: Selecting a procedure does not grant authorization.

relationships.subject: skill-replacement
relationships.definition: The explicit replacement applies to every declared loading route.

relationships.subject: skill-extension
relationships.definition: The declared order retains the base procedure.

relationships.subject: resident-composition
relationships.definition: The final composed context is measured and scoped.

relationships.subject: evidence
relationships.definition: A runtime claim needs evidence from the actual registered path.

relationships.subject: evidence
relationships.definition: A passing schema or an installed hook alone cannot support this claim.

relationships.subject: authorization-record
relationships.definition: The issuer authority and scope are established outside this registry.

relationships.subject: rollback-receipt
relationships.definition: Rollback identifies an exact compatible set rather than a moving branch tip.

relationships.subject: effective-policy
relationships.definition: Authorized workflow configuration cannot weaken the shared integrity requirements.

relationships.subject: generated-artifact
relationships.definition: Composed managed artifacts must identify one compatible immutable parent; a mixed-lock result is invalid.
